title: How Copy, Paste, Go works — and pick your project
goal: Your orientation: what the 30 days hold, how stages, days, chapters and lessons fit together, what's inside a lesson, how tasks are reviewed, how the agent kit unlocks and how achievements work. Then you pick your project and set up.

processes.title: Kick-off
processes.summary: Understand the month, pick your project, set up your agent and kit.

lessons.title: Welcome to Copy, Paste, Go
lessons.summary: What the 30 days are for, and the road ahead.
objectives: What the 30 days are for, and the road ahead.
lessons.exercise: In two or three lines: what do you want to be able to do on Day 30 that you can't do today? Keep it — you'll come back to it at the capstone.
criteria: I know what I'll make this month
I've written what I want from it

guide.intro: In 30 days you take one real project from idea to a running, measured product — working the way modern teams do, with AI agents as your team. You decide; your agents draft, research and check.

sections.title: The road ahead
sections.body: Ten stages, in order. Each one asks a question, ends at a gate, and hands its results to the next. 182 lessons in all.

stages.name: Kick-off
stages.line: Learn how the month works, pick your project, set up.

stages.name: Discover
stages.line: What's really there — and can we build it?

stages.name: Capstone
stages.line: Pull your evidence together, present, earn the certificate.

sections.title: Three tracks
sections.body: The stages sit in three tracks — the way real delivery teams work, not one long waterfall.
points: Discovery
Discover · Plan · Design — are we building the right thing?
Delivery
Build · Verify · Release — are we building the thing right?
Run & learn
Operate · Evolve — is it working, and what did we learn?

sections.title: What you leave with
points: A shipped project
One project, carried through every stage — with every document, decision and result as evidence.
A portfolio
Your project folder is the portfolio: it shows how you think, not just what you built.
The certificate
Earned at the capstone, after you present your project to a mentor.
Your agent kit
Every stage's prompts, commands, skills and reviewers — yours to keep using.

guide.intro: The month is built in layers. Big picture first, then down to the single step you're doing now.

sections.title: What opens what
points: Days
A day opens when you finish the day before it. Finish a day by completing its lessons and ticking its gate.
Stages
A stage opens on its first day — with its chapters, its lessons and its agent kit.
Gates
Each stage ends at a gate (Discovery Decision, Commitment, Definition of Done…). You check its criteria before moving on — just as a real team would.

sections.title: Two ways to see it
points: Now & next
My program shows the stage you're in, what's up next, and what comes later.
The full map
Every day on one road, through the three tracks — with your progress drawn in.

guide.intro: Every lesson from Day 1 on has the same shape, so after the first one you always know where you are.

steps.name: Learn
steps.what: A guided walk through the lesson, one idea at a time.

steps.name: Overview
steps.what: What it's for, the outcome, who's involved.

steps.name: Workflow
steps.what: The map of how the work flows.

steps.name: Contract
steps.what: Inputs, outputs, owners, rules and the checks.

steps.name: Artifacts
steps.what: The documents it makes — with ready templates.

steps.name: Knowledge
steps.what: The frameworks, techniques and lenses it uses.

steps.name: Do it
steps.what: Your tasks, on your project — then hand them in.

sections.title: Reading a workflow map
sections.body: This is a real one — “Read the Brief”, from Day 1. Steps run left to right to the gate. A diamond is a decision. The loops are what happens when things don't go to plan.

loops.label: Conflicts with a hard limit → client

sections.title: Lenses
sections.body: Every lesson is also seen through lenses — privacy, security, cost, accessibility and more. They're the questions an expert in that area would ask, so nothing important gets missed.

lessons.title: Tasks, submissions and reviews
lessons.summary: What you make in each lesson, and how it gets checked.
objectives: What you make in each lesson, and how it gets checked.
lessons.exercise: Read the cycle below. Then write one line on why you score your own work before you hand it in.
criteria: I know how a task goes from draft to approved
I know where my submissions live

guide.intro: Every lesson asks you to make something real for your project — a document, a canvas, a register. You play the role; a reviewer plays the people you hand it to.

steps.name: Draft
steps.what: Fill the template in the lesson — your agent helps.

steps.name: Self-check
steps.what: Tick the subtasks, score yourself on the rubric.

steps.name: Hand in
steps.what: Send it to the role who receives it.

steps.name: Review
steps.what: A mentor grades it on the same rubric.

steps.name: Approved
steps.what: 80% or more on the rubric, with no zeros.

back.name: Sent back
back.what: With comments. Fix it and hand it in again.

sections.title: Where your work lives
points: Living documents
Logs, registers and canvases grow lesson by lesson — you keep adding to the same document all month.
Submissions
My program → Submissions shows every document and where it stands: draft, in review, approved or to fix.
Your progress
Your profile shows grades, first-time passes, and how close your self-scores are to the reviewer's.

sections.title: Good to know
points: Score honestly
Self-scores close to the reviewer's earn the “Honest scorer” badge — and teach you what good looks like.
Sent back isn't failing
Fixing work and getting it approved is part of the job — it even has its own badge.

objectives: The files that turn your AI agent into a team — and how they unlock.
lessons.exercise: Get access to an AI agent (for example a Claude Pro or Max plan with Claude Code, or the API) and have one short conversation with it. Then make a project folder with a docs/ folder, and copy the kick-off kit's root files into it from the Agent kit page.
criteria: My AI agent is set up and I've tested it
My project folder is ready, with the kit in it

guide.intro: Copy, Paste, Go is named after the kit: for every stage you get ready-made files your agent can use straight away — or configure your way.

sections.title: What's in a stage's kit — Discover has 338 files

layers.name: AGENTS.md
layers.what: What your agent always knows about your project.

layers.name: Commands
layers.what: Saved prompts — one for every step and lesson.

layers.name: Workflows
layers.what: Run specs with checkpoints where you decide.

layers.name: Subagents
layers.what: Reviewers and helpers with one job each.

layers.name: Guardrails
layers.what: Rules and checks your agent follows.

sections.title: How it unlocks
sections.body: Each stage's kit opens on its first day — so you're never buried in files you don't need yet. Inside a lesson, the Agent tab shows just the files that task uses — open them in the kit and copy what you need. The kit stays on Copy, Paste, Go and is for members only.

stages.name: Discover
stages.line: What's really there — and can we build it?

sections.title: Working with your agent
points: You decide
Your agent drafts, researches, checks and challenges. You make the calls and own the result.
Check everything
Score its drafts against the rubric. Correct what it gets wrong — that's the habit for the whole month.
Any agent
The kit works with any agent — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, a chat assistant. Some features (skills, subagents, hooks) need agents that support them.
Yours alone
The kit is licensed to you. Please don't share it.

guide.intro: Real progress is the shipped project — but it helps to see it add up, and to have people around you.

sections.title: XP and levels
sections.body: Everything you do earns XP. XP raises your level, and levels unlock titles and avatar frames.

rows: Answer a question on the board

sections.title: Badges and the leaderboard
points: Badges
Kicked off, First approval, Right first time, On a roll, Comeback, Helper… many have bronze, silver and gold tiers.
Streak
Work on consecutive days to grow your streak — one missed day a week is forgiven.
Leaderboard
A weekly season resets every Monday. Top the week to be crowned Champion; the top three wear a shining title. You can hide yourself if you prefer.

sections.title: You're not alone
points: Feed
What the cohort is up to — wins, questions, shares.
Board
Ask about any day or lesson; others answer, mentors step in.
Live sessions
Mentor sessions through the month — vote for the time that suits you.

guide.intro: Everything you make this month is for one project. Choose one you'll stay curious about for 30 days.

sections.title: Choosing well
points: A real problem
Someone, somewhere, wastes time or money on it today.
People you can picture
You can name who's affected and who'd pay or sponsor the fix.
Small enough to ship
One problem, done well — not a whole platform.
Not sure?
Pick a practice project below. Each comes with a client brief, people and numbers, ready to go.
